State significant infrastructure approved under Part 5.1 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

In this Division, a reference to action being, or about to be, carried out includes a reference to action that should be, but is not being, carried out and an order under this Division may be modified accordingly.
A person must not—
contravene an order under this section, or
cause or permit another person to contravene such an order.
Maximum penalty (subsection (6))—
in the case of a corporation—10,000 penalty units and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further penalty of 1,000 penalty units for each day the offence continues, or
in the case of an individual—1,000 penalty units and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further penalty of 100 penalty units for each day the offence continues.

An offence against subsection (6) committed by a corporation is an executive liability offence attracting executive liability for a director or other person involved in the management of the corporation—see section 175B.

heading.b: Prior notification of making of stop work order not required

block.txt: The Secretary is not required, before making an order under this Division, to notify any person who may be affected by the order.
A person against whom an order is made under this Division may appeal to the Minister against the making of the order.
After hearing an appeal, the Minister may—
confirm the order, or

modify or rescind the order, but only if this is consistent with the principles of ecologically sustainable development (as described in section 6 (2) of the Protection of the Environment Administration Act 1991).
The Secretary may extend an order under this Division for such further period or periods of 40 days as the Secretary thinks fit.

heading.b: Consultation about modification of proposed detrimental action

block.txt: After making an order under this Division, the Secretary must immediately consult with the person proposing to perform the action to determine whether any modification of the action may be sufficient to protect the environment of any protected fauna or native plants.

If, in the opinion of the Secretary, satisfactory arrangements cannot be made to protect the environment that is the subject of an order under this Division, the Secretary must recommend the making of an interim protection order under Division 2.

The Secretary must not recommend the making of an interim protection order in relation to anything that is authorised to be done by or under an authority referred to in section 91AA (3) or that is essential for a purpose referred to in section 91AA (4).

If an order under this Division is in force in relation to an environment, an approval, notice or order (whether made or issued before or after the order pursuant to this Division) under any other Act that requires or permits the environment to be significantly affected is inoperative to the extent of the inconsistency with the order.
This section has effect whether the approval, notice, order or other instrument concerned was made before or after the making of the order under this Division.

content.txt: pt 6A, div 2, hdg: Ins 1995 No 101, Sch 4 [52].

heading.b: Interim protection of areas having significant values

block.txt: The Secretary may recommend to the Minister the making of an interim protection order in respect of an area of land—
which has, in the Secretary’s opinion, natural, scientific or cultural significance, or

on which the Secretary intends to exercise any of the Secretary’s powers, authorities, duties or functions under this Act or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 relating to fauna, native plants, threatened species, populations or ecological communities or critical habitat of endangered species, populations or ecological communities, or
that is critical habitat or the habitat of a threatened species, population or ecological community.

After the commencement of Part 11 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016, a recommendation for the making of an interim protection order may not be made except in relation to areas of cultural significance.
The Minister may, after considering a recommendation made under section 91A, make an interim protection order in respect of the area of land the subject of the recommendation.
An interim protection order shall take effect on the date of its publication in the Gazette or on a later date specified in the order.

An interim protection order may contain terms of a kind set out in the regulations, being terms relating to the preservation, protection and maintenance of the area of land, its fauna, plants, threatened species, populations and ecological communities and critical habitat of endangered species, populations and ecological communities and any Aboriginal object or place subject to the order.

heading.b: Notice of intention to make order not required

block.txt: The Minister is not required, before making an interim protection order, to notify any person who will be affected by the order of the intention to make the order.
An interim protection order has effect for such period, being not longer than 2 years, as is specified in the order.
An order ceases to have effect if the area of land subject to the order is reserved or dedicated under this Act or the order is revoked.
The Minister may revoke an interim protection order by notice of revocation.
A notice of revocation shall take effect on the date of its publication in the Gazette or on a later date specified in the notice.

heading.b: Notice of making of interim protection order

block.txt: The Minister shall cause notice of an interim protection order and its terms or of the revocation of such an order to be given, as soon as practicable after its publication in the Gazette, to—
any person who appears to the Minister to be an owner or occupier of the area of land subject to the order,
the Council,
the council in whose area (within the meaning of the Local Government Act 1993) the area of land subject to the order is situated, and
any other person the Minister thinks fit,
and shall consider any advice given by the Council relating to the order.

heading.b: Failure to comply with interim protection order

block.txt: A person who is given notice of an interim protection order under section 91F must not—
contravene the terms of the order, or
cause or permit another person to contravene the terms of the order.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—10,000 penalty units and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further penalty of 1,000 penalty units for each day the offence continues, or
in the case of an individual—1,000 penalty units and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further penalty of 100 penalty units for each day the offence continues.

An offence against this section committed by a corporation is an executive liability offence attracting executive liability for a director or other person involved in the management of the corporation—see section 175B.

An owner or occupier of the whole or any part of an area of land subject to an interim protection order may appeal to the Land and Environment Court against the imposition of the order or any of its terms.
Such an appeal shall be made within the time and in the manner provided by the rules of the Court.
In deciding an appeal, the Court may have regard to—
any hardship caused to the owner or occupier by the imposition of the order or any of its terms, and
the purposes of the order.
In deciding such an appeal, the Court has all the functions and discretions of the Minister under this Part and may make such order as it thinks fit.
A decision of the Court on an appeal is final and shall be given effect to as if it were the decision of the Minister.
The Secretary shall keep a register containing copies of interim protection orders as in force from time to time.
The register shall be open for public inspection during ordinary business hours, and copies of or extracts from the register shall be available, on payment of the fee fixed by the Secretary.

After the commencement of Part 11 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016, a direction under this Division may not be given except in relation to any land reserved under this Act or acquired under Part 11 or any Aboriginal object or Aboriginal place.
In this Division—
damage—
in relation to land reserved under this Act or acquired under Part 11, includes—
harming an animal, or picking a plant, that is in or on that land, or
damming, diverting or polluting any waters on that land, or
damage to anything in or on the land (such as a building, structure, pipe, sign, gate, fence etc or any object or place of cultural value), or
removal of anything, or part of anything, in or on the land, and
in relation to a plant, includes picking the plant, and
in relation to an animal, includes harming the animal.
landholder means a person who owns land or who, whether by reason of ownership or otherwise, is in lawful occupation or possession, or has lawful management or control, of land.
pollute waters has the same meaning as in the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997.
waters includes a stream, creek, river, estuary, dam, lake or reservoir.

heading.b: Directions for remedial work relating to damage to land, habitat and plants and animals

block.txt: The Secretary may, by notice in writing, direct a person to carry out specified remediation work in a specified manner and within a specified time, if the Secretary is satisfied that—
any land reserved under this Act or acquired under Part 11, or
any critical habitat, or habitat of threatened species, an endangered population or an endangered ecological community, or
any plant or animal that is of, or is part of, a threatened species, an endangered population or an endangered ecological community,
has been damaged in or as a result of the commission of an offence under this Act (whether or not any person has been proceeded against or convicted for the offence).
The specified remediation work to be carried out by a person may include one or more of the following types of work—
work to control, abate or mitigate the damage to the land, habitat, plant or animal concerned,
work to maintain, remediate or restore the damaged land, habitat, plant or animal concerned (including replacing removed or dead plants or animals).
A direction under this section may be varied or revoked by a further notice in writing.

heading.b: Directions for remedial work relating to harm to Aboriginal objects and places

block.txt: The Secretary may, by notice in writing, direct a person to carry out specified remediation work in a specified manner and within a specified time, if the Secretary is satisfied that—
any Aboriginal object, or
any Aboriginal place,
has been harmed in or as a result of the commission of an offence under this Act (whether or not any person has been proceeded against or convicted for the offence).
The specified remediation work to be carried out by a person may include one or more of the following types of work—
work to control, abate or mitigate the harm to the Aboriginal object or Aboriginal place concerned,
work to protect, conserve, maintain, remediate or restore the harmed Aboriginal object or Aboriginal place concerned.
A direction under this section may be varied or revoked by a further notice in writing.

heading.b: Persons to whom directions may be given

block.txt: A direction under this Division may be given to any or all of the following persons—
the current or former landholder of any land affected by the damage or harm referred to in section 91K or 91L or on which such damage or harm occurred,
any other person the Secretary reasonably believes is responsible for that damage or harm or caused or permitted that damage or harm.

heading.b: Other ancillary actions that may be directed to be carried out

block.txt: The Secretary in a direction under this Division may also direct a person to carry out the following actions—
ascertaining the nature and extent of the damage or harm concerned and furnishing the information or records obtained to other persons (including to the Secretary),
preparing, furnishing and carrying out a plan of action,
furnishing progress reports,
monitoring, sampling and analysing anything to ascertain the nature and extent of the harm concerned or the progress in remediating the harm,
vacating the land concerned (or part of it), ceasing to carry on, modifying, or not commencing, an activity on, or use of, the land (or part of it),
carrying on an activity (or an aspect of it) only during particular times or in a particular manner,
in relation to harm to an Aboriginal object or place, preparing a report on an activity’s likely impact on the Aboriginal object or Aboriginal place concerned,
construction, installation or removal of anything (including plants and structures such as fencing, walls, bunds or other barriers),

erecting or displaying on the land concerned any sign or notice containing directions to persons not to enter the land or not to use the land in a specified manner or for a specified purpose or containing other directions of that kind or any other kind,
refraining from disturbance or further disturbance of the land concerned in a specified manner or below a specified depth,
informing the Secretary of any change in the ownership or occupancy of the land concerned, to the extent that the person subject to the requirement is aware of the change,
in relation to harm to an Aboriginal object or place, consulting with Aboriginal community groups or representatives (for example to develop a strategy or plan in relation to the remediation work),
in relation to harm to an Aboriginal object, moving the object.

heading.b: Other person may carry out remediation work if failure to comply with direction

block.txt: If a person fails to comply with a direction under section 91K or 91L, the Secretary may direct any other person to enter the land concerned and carry out all or part of the specified work.
The Secretary may recover the cost of that work from the person given the direction in any court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due by that person to the Crown.

heading.b: Entry to land to carry out direction

block.txt: A person may enter land to carry out a direction under this Division.
Nothing in this Division authorises a person to enter any part of premises used only for residential purposes except with the consent of the occupier of the premises.

heading.b: Failure to comply with remediation direction

block.txt: A person must not, without reasonable excuse—
contravene a direction under this Division, or
cause or permit another person to contravene such a direction.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—2,000 penalty units and 200 penalty units for each day the offence continues, or
in any other case—1,000 penalty units and 100 penalty units for each day the offence continues.

An offence against subsection (1) committed by a corporation is an executive liability offence attracting executive liability for a director or other person involved in the management of the corporation—see section 175B.

For the purposes of subsection (1), an example of a reasonable excuse is that the person was unable to enter land because of the refusal of access to the land by its occupier, but entry to that land was essential for the person to avoid committing the relevant offence.

heading.b: Delay or obstruction of remediation direction

block.txt: A person must not wilfully delay or obstruct another person—
who is carrying out any action in compliance with a direction under this Division, or
who is authorised to enter land and carry out work under this Division.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—2,000 penalty units and 200 penalty units for each day the offence continues, or
in any other case—1,000 penalty units and 100 penalty units for each day the offence continues.

An offence against this section committed by a corporation is an executive liability offence attracting executive liability for a director or other person involved in the management of the corporation—see section 175B.

If the person given a direction under this Division complies with the direction but was not the person who caused the damage or harm concerned, the cost of complying with the direction may be recovered by the person who complied with the direction as a debt in a court of competent jurisdiction from the person who caused the damage or harm.
A person given a direction under this Division may appeal against the direction to the Land and Environment Court within 30 days of the service of the notice of the direction.
The lodging of an appeal does not, except to the extent that the Land and Environment Court otherwise directs in relation to the appeal, operate to stay action on the direction appealed against.

heading.b: National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Trust

block.txt: In this Part—
ITAA 1997 means the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 of the Commonwealth.
Operating Fund means the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Operating Fund established under section 108(1).
Public Fund—see section 105(1).
Trust means the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Trust established under section 93.

heading.b: Establishment, functions and operation of Trust

block.txt: There is established by this Act a body corporate with the corporate name of the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Trust of New South Wales.
The Trust is a statutory body representing the Crown.
The Trust is subject to the control and direction of the Minister, except in relation to payments from the Public Fund and the Operating Fund.
The Trust must publish directions given to the Trust by the Minister on the Trust’s website.
There is to be a Board of the Trust.
The Board of the Trust must consist of at least 5, and no more than 11, members appointed by the Minister.
The affairs of the Trust are to be managed by the Board.
An act, matter or thing done in the name of, or on behalf of, the Trust by the Board is taken to have been done by the Trust.
The Minister may do the following, in accordance with the regulations in relation to the Board—
appoint members of the Board, including persons with skills and experience in areas the Minister considers relevant,
appoint a Chairperson and a Deputy Chairperson of the Board,
determine remuneration and entitlements for travelling or other expenses for members of the Board,
remove a member of the Board from office,
establish committees and procedures for the committees,
dissolve the Board.
The regulations may make provisions about the following—
the composition of the membership of the Board appointed by the Minister,
procedures for nominations to the Board,
procedures for the administration of membership of the Board, including the term of office for members of the Board,
the procedures for—
calling of meetings of the Board, and
conducting business at the meetings, including procedures to be determined by the Board,
procedures in relation to possible conflicts of interest,
the application of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 to members of the Board,
fees that may be determined by the Board for services,
requirements for the seal of the Trust,
the dissolution of the Board.

The object of the Trust is to support and promote the protection and enhancement of the natural environment through the use of gifts of money and property received by the Public Fund, and money held by the Operating Fund, by supporting the following actions, if the actions are in addition to actions that are or would ordinarily be taken—
the acquisition of lands under this Act,
scientific research and monitoring,
threatened species conservation, including restoration,
projects that support the involvement of Aboriginal people in park management, including joint management,
activities or classes of activities prescribed by the regulations, other than activities that are part of routine land management or routine visitor management.
The Trust is not-for-profit.
The object of the Trust is also its principal purpose.

For donations to the Public Fund to have tax deductible status under the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 of the Commonwealth, Subdivision 30-E, the Trust must have as its principal purpose the protection and enhancement of the natural environment or of a significant aspect of the natural environment.
The Trust has the following functions—
to establish and maintain the Public Fund,
to administer the Operating Fund, including to make payments into and out of the Operating Fund in accordance with Division 4,
to invite and encourage members of the public and organisations to make gifts of money and property to the Public Fund,
to establish and maintain a website for the purposes of facilitating the functions of the Trust,
to use the following to support and promote the actions specified in section 96(1)(a)–(e) to the extent the actions promote the protection and enhancement of the natural environment—
gifts, devises, bequests or contributions received by the Public Fund,
money held in the Operating Fund,
to assess and analyse lands for potential acquisition by payments from the Public Fund and the Operating Fund,
to invest money held in the Public Fund and the Operating Fund,
to exercise functions delegated to the Trust under this Act,
another function conferred or imposed on the Trust by this Act or another law.

The Trust has power to do all things that are necessary or convenient to be done for or in connection with the exercise of its functions or that are supplemental or incidental to, or consequential on, the exercise of its functions.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Trust has power to do the following—
to buy, sell, hold, mortgage, lease or otherwise deal with land or other property,
to borrow money, either with or without security,
to act as trustee of money or other property vested in the Trust,
to invest money held in the Public Fund and the Operating Fund—
if the Trust is a GSF agency for the purposes of the Government Sector Finance Act 2018, Part 6—in a way that the Trust is permitted to invest money under that Part, or
if the Trust is not a GSF agency for the purposes of the Government Sector Finance Act 2018, Part 6—in the same way as trustees may invest trust funds or in another way approved by the Treasurer,
to make and enter into contracts or other arrangements for the carrying out of works, the performance of services or the supply of goods or materials,
to appoint agents,
to set fees in relation to administrative matters.
Persons may be employed in the Public Service under the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 to enable the Trust to exercise its functions.

The Government Sector Employment Act 2013, section 59 provides that the persons employed, or whose services the Trust makes use of, may be referred to as officers or employees, or members of staff, of the Trust. The Constitution Act 1902, section 47A precludes the Trust from employing staff.
The Trust may engage consultants for the purpose of getting expert advice.
The Trust may delegate a function of the Trust, other than this power of delegation, to—
a member of the Board of the Trust, or
an employee of the Trust, or
a person, or a person of a class, prescribed by the regulations.

The regulations may prescribe additional matters relating to the exercise of the Trust’s functions that the Trust is required to include in the annual reporting information prepared for the Trust under the Government Sector Finance Act 2018.
The Duties Act 1997 does not apply to or in relation to—
the acquisition of land by the Trust for the purposes of this Act, or
the leasing of land, whether as lessor or lessee, by the Trust for the purposes of this Act, or
the disposal of land by the Trust under this Act.

heading.b: National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Public Fund

block.txt: In this Division—
Environment Secretary has the same meaning as in the ITAA 1997.

heading.b: Registration of Trust as environmental organisation

block.txt: The Trust must comply with the requirements set out in the ITAA 1997, Subdivision 30-E in relation to the Trust’s registration as an environmental organisation within the meaning of the ITAA 1997.
In particular, the Trust must—
establish and maintain a not-for-profit public fund that meets the requirements of the ITAA 1997, section 30-130, in accordance with section 105, and
comply with a rule the Commonwealth Minister and the Environment Minister make to ensure that gifts made to the public fund are used only for the principal purpose of the Trust, and
not pay any of the Trust’s profits or financial surplus, or give any of the Trust’s property, to its members, and
not act as a mere conduit for the donation of money or property to other organisations, bodies or persons, and
agree to give the Environment Secretary, within a reasonable period after the end of each income year, statistical information about gifts made to the Public Fund during the income year.
In this section—
Commonwealth Minister means a Commonwealth Minister responsible for administering the relevant provisions of the ITAA 1997.
Environment Minister has the same meaning as in the ITAA 1997.

heading.b: National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Public Fund

block.txt: The public fund referred to in section 104(2)(a) must be called the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Public Fund (the Public Fund).
The Trust must—
maintain and only use the Public Fund for the principal purpose of the Trust, and
hold all accountable gifts in the Public Fund, and
not hold other money or property in the Public Fund, and
pay all money held in the Public Fund into an account kept, for the purposes of the Public Fund, with an authorised deposit-taking institution, and

keep records that record and explain all transactions and other acts the Trust engages in that are relevant to the Trust’s endorsement as a deductible gift recipient for operating the Public Fund, and
The Taxation Administration Act 1953 of the Commonwealth, Schedule 1, section 382-15 requires deductible gift recipients to keep certain records.
issue receipts in the name of the Public Fund for accountable gifts worth $2 or more, and

notify the Australian Taxation Office and the Environment Secretary of any changes made to the provisions of this Act that relate to the Trust or the Public Fund after the Trust is registered as an environmental organisation under the ITAA 1997, Subdivision 30-E.
In this section—
accountable gifts means gifts, property, contributions or money referred to in the ITAA 1997, section 30-130.
authorised deposit-taking institution has the same meaning as ADI has in the ITAA 1997.

heading.b: Transfer of assets on winding up

block.txt: At the first occurrence of a winding up event, the Trust must transfer surplus assets of the Public Fund that can be deducted under the ITAA 1997, Division 30 to a tax exempt fund determined by the Minister.
The Minister must give preference to tax exempt funds that operate principally in New South Wales.
In this section—
tax exempt fund means a public fund that is—
on the register of environmental organisations kept under the ITAA 1997, Subdivision 30-E, and
maintained for a similar purpose to the principal purpose of the Trust.
winding up event means—
the winding up of the Trust, or
the winding up of the Public Fund, or
the revocation of the Trust’s endorsement as a deductible gift recipient under the ITAA 1997, Division 30.

The regulations may make provisions about matters necessary to ensure compliance with a requirement under the ITAA 1997 for the proper functioning of the Trust as a registered environmental organisation under the ITAA 1997, including in relation to—
additional administrative arrangements to address a requirement, or
additional governance arrangements to address a requirement.

heading.b: National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Operating Fund
National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Operating Fund

block.txt: There is to be established in the Special Deposits Account a fund called the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Operating Fund.
The Operating Fund must be administered by the Trust.
The purpose of the Operating Fund is to hold money for the exercise of the Trust’s functions.
The Operating Fund may hold money the Public Fund cannot hold because of the requirements of the ITAA 1997.
The following must be paid into the Operating Fund—
money appropriated by Parliament for the purposes of the Operating Fund,
money, including money from grants and contributions, that cannot otherwise be held by the Public Fund,
the proceeds of the investment of money in the Operating Fund,
money authorised by the Treasurer to be paid into the Operating Fund,
money directed or authorised to be paid into the Operating Fund by or under this Act or another Act or law.
The following are payable from the Operating Fund—
money required to support and promote the actions specified in section 96(1)(a)–(e) to the extent the actions promote the protection and enhancement of the natural environment,
money required to meet expenses in relation to the administration of the Operating Fund,
money required to meet expenses in relation to the exercise of the Trust’s functions.

content.txt: pt 9, hdg: Subst 2002 No 78, Sch 2.5 [36]. Rep 2016 No 63, Sch 11.5 [15].

block.txt: The National Parks and Wildlife Fund established under the Act of 1967 shall continue in existence and shall be kept at the Treasury in the Special Deposits Account.
There shall be paid into the Fund—

all money provided by Parliament for the purposes of this Act (including money provided for the expenses incurred or likely to be incurred by boards of management in connection with the preparation of plans of management for, and the care, control and management of, lands reserved or dedicated under Part 4A), the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 (except any money provided by Parliament for the purposes of the Biodiversity Banking Account or Biobanking Trust Fund under Part 7A of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995),
all money provided by Parliament for the management of any land for which the National Parks and Wildlife Reserve Trust is the Crown land manager,
all money received in respect of—

leases, licences, permits or occupancies within a national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve, Aboriginal area or land for which the National Parks and Wildlife Reserve Trust is the Crown land manager,
the creation of and dealing with carbon sequestration rights in land acquired, reserved or dedicated under this Act,
leases and licences granted under section 149 (4),

royalties, fees and charges under this Act or the regulations, the Wilderness Act 1987, the Snowy Mountains Cloud Seeding Act 2004 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 or the regulations made under those Acts, except those that are required to be paid into the Biodiversity Banking Account or Biobanking Trust Fund under Part 7A of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995,
despite the provisions of any other Act, royalties, fees and charges in respect of land for which the National Parks and Wildlife Reserve Trust is the Crown land manager,
franchises granted under section 152,
easements or rights of way granted under section 153,
community service contributions,

penalties recovered pursuant to this Act or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 or the regulations made under those Acts, or (despite the provisions of any other Act) under another Act in respect of land for which the National Parks and Wildlife Reserve Trust is the Crown land manager, except penalties recovered pursuant to Part 7A of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 or the regulations under that Part,
property forfeited pursuant to this Act or the regulations,
costs paid pursuant to an order under section 176 (3),
amounts paid pursuant to an order under section 177, and

policies of insurance under which money is paid to the Minister or the Secretary with respect to any national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve or Aboriginal area, or any property in the custody or under the control of the Secretary,
all money received in respect of—
rent paid by the Minister in respect of lands leased under Part 4A, and
matters of a kind referred to in paragraph (b) in respect of those lands,
any money acquired by the Minister pursuant to section 148, except money required to be paid into the Biodiversity Banking Account under Part 7A of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995,
any money received by the Minister pursuant to section 149, except money required to be paid into the Biodiversity Banking Account under Part 7A of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995,

any other money received in connection with any national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve or Aboriginal area or any proposed national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve or Aboriginal area,
any money received from the Sydney Catchment Authority in connection with carrying out and giving effect to a plan of management adopted under the Sydney Water Catchment Management Act 1998,

any money received by the Secretary or a board of management in connection with an order of a court under section 201, 203 or 204 of this Act or section 141J, 141L or 141M of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995,
any money received in connection with any wildlife refuge or conservation area, and

any other money received in connection with the administration of this Act, the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995, other than money received in the prescribed circumstances (if any) or money payable into the Biodiversity Banking Account or Biobanking Trust Fund under Part 7A of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995.
Within the Fund there is to be a separate account for each area of lands leased under Part 4A.

Subject to subsections (2) and (3), any money paid into the Fund, including rent paid by the Minister, in respect of an area of lands leased under Part 4A is to be carried into the separate account in the Fund that relates to that area.

Any money referred to in subsection (1B) may, pending its application in accordance with this Act, be invested by the Minister with the Treasurer or in any manner in which trustees are for the time being authorised to invest trust funds.

Where any money acquired by the Minister pursuant to section 148 is subject to any condition to which the Minister has agreed, the money shall be carried to a separate account in the Fund and shall be applied in accordance with the condition.

Any money referred to in subsection (2) may, pending application in accordance with the condition so referred to, be invested by the Minister with the Treasurer or in any manner in which trustees are for the time being authorised to invest trust funds.

A reference in subsection (1) (b) (i) or (e) to a regional park does not include a reference to a regional park that is, or is proposed to be, under the care, control and management of a local council.

Money received in connection with the administration of the biodiversity certification scheme (including any fees paid under the scheme or any monetary contributions made for the purposes of the scheme) is not to be paid into the National Parks and Wildlife Fund.
In this section—
biodiversity certification scheme means—
the provisions of Part 7AA of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 and any regulations made for the purposes of that Part, and
the provisions of Parts 7 and 8 of Schedule 7 to that Act (which relate to biodiversity certification of environmental planning instruments).
No money shall be paid out of the Fund except under the authority of this Act or in accordance with section 52 (2) (b) of the Fire and Rescue NSW Act 1989.
There may be paid out of the Fund—

all charges, costs and expenses incurred by the Minister or the Secretary in exercising and performing the Minister’s or the Secretary’s powers, authorities, duties and functions under this Act, the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995, except those incurred under the biodiversity certification scheme and the biobanking scheme,
all money allocated by the Minister for expenditure by a state conservation area trust in connection with a state conservation area or by a regional park trust in connection with a regional park,
all charges, costs and expenses incurred by the National Parks and Wildlife Reserve Trust in exercising its functions in relation to land for which it is the Crown land manager,
the fees and travelling and other expenses payable to the members of the Council or any committee under this Act, the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995,
the cost of acquiring land for the purposes of this Act, the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995,

the cost of improvement of any land adjoining or in the vicinity of a national park, historic site, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve, Aboriginal area or state conservation area, where in the opinion of the Minister this is desirable to provide or improve access to the park, site, reserve or area, or to provide or improve facilities or amenities for persons visiting the park, site, reserve or area,
all money which the Minister directs shall be set aside to provide a reserve for insurance,
all money allocated by the Minister for expenditure on Aboriginal areas,
the cost of the Minister creating and dealing with carbon sequestration rights in land acquired, reserved or dedicated under this Act,
the cost of acquiring Aboriginal objects or land in which Aboriginal objects or Aboriginal places are situated,
the cost of erecting and maintaining buildings or structures for the safe custody, storage or exhibition of any Aboriginal object,
the cost of entering into, and giving effect to, agreements under sections 145 and 146,
the cost of carrying out the purposes for which land is acquired or occupied under section 146,

all costs incurred under sections 147 and 149 (except in relation to a dealing in land or other property, or an interest in property, the proceeds of which are payable into the Biodiversity Banking Account under Part 7A of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995),
charges, costs and expenses incurred in the administration of the Marine Estate Management Act 2014,
the cost of carrying out and giving effect to a plan of management adopted under the Sydney Water Catchment Management Act 1998,
charges, costs and expenses incurred by the Service in connection with cloud seeding operations authorised by the Snowy Mountains Cloud Seeding Act 2004,
all money allocated by the Minister for use in connection with a wildlife refuge or conservation area,
all money to be paid to Local Land Services under section 141, and
any other costs, charges, expenses, money or fees prescribed by the regulations.

Any money set aside, as referred to in subsection (2) (f), may be invested by the Minister with the Treasurer or in any manner in which trustees are for the time being authorised to invest trust funds.
Where—
any lands are acquired under Part 11 out of money wholly or partly provided by Parliament, and
those lands, or any part thereof, are sold under section 149,
there shall be paid from the Fund to the Treasurer, out of the proceeds of the sale referred to in paragraph (b), such amount as the Treasurer may determine.
Any money in a separate account kept under section 138 (1B) in respect of lands reserved or dedicated under Part 4A must be applied—
for the management of the lands (including the preparation of a plan of management for the lands), and
in accordance with the provisions of any plan of management for the lands.
In this section—
biobanking scheme means the provisions of Part 7A of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 and any regulations made for the purposes of that Part.
biodiversity certification scheme means—
the provisions of Part 7AA of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 and any regulations made for the purposes of that Part, and
the provisions of Parts 7 and 8 of Schedule 7 to that Act (which relate to biodiversity certification of environmental planning instruments).

The Secretary shall from time to time assess the amount of the contribution to be paid by the holder of a lease of or licence to occupy or use lands within a national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve or karst conservation reserve for the cost of providing or maintaining any community service in the park, site, area or reserve.
The Secretary may levy the contribution payable by the holder of the lease or licence by serving on the holder a written notice of the contribution payable.
The notice referred to in subsection (2) may—
relate to one or more types of community service, and
specify a date by which the contribution must be paid.
The amount of the contribution is due and payable to, and is recoverable by, the Secretary—
if a date is specified in the notice referred to in subsection (2)—on that date, or
if no such date is specified—on the expiration of one month from the service of the notice.
Nothing in this section prevents the Secretary from issuing separate notices to the same holder of a lease or licence for different types of community service.
The Minister, on the recommendation of the Secretary, may for any reason which to the Minister seems sufficient exempt any such holder from the payment of such a contribution or part thereof.
In this section, community service includes the following actions or services when undertaken or provided in connection with public health or building safety—
making an inspection,
conducting an audit,
receiving an application,
granting an approval.

heading.b: Payment of rates to Local Land Services in Western Division

block.txt: An amount is, subject to this section, payable to Local Land Services equal to the amount that would have been payable to Local Land Services under Part 5 (Rates, levies and contributions) of the Local Land Services Act 2013 by way of rates for any period, in respect of land reserved as national parks or historic sites or dedicated as nature reserves or karst conservation reserves, had the land been rateable land under that Act at all relevant times after they were so reserved or dedicated.
No amount is payable under subsection (2) except upon an application—
made to the Secretary in the prescribed manner and within the prescribed time, and
containing the prescribed particulars.

Any dispute between the Secretary and Local Land Services with respect to the particulars contained in an application or the amount payable under this section shall be determined in accordance with such directions as the Minister, after consultation with the Minister for Agriculture, may give.
Nothing in this section requires or authorises the payment of an amount in relation to any period before the commencement day.
Royalty shall, in accordance with the regulations, be payable to the Crown at the prescribed rates upon such species of fauna and the skins of such species of fauna as may be prescribed.

Notwithstanding subsection (1), royalty shall not be payable under this section in respect of a skin or carcase to which there has been affixed or attached in compliance with a condition of a licence issued under Division 2 of Part 9 a label, tag, slip or other object for which a charge or fee has been paid pursuant to regulations made under section 154 (e).
Where the Minister, the Secretary or an officer of the Service—
supplies any service, product or commodity,
grants any licence to carry on a trade, business or occupation,
gives, varies or transfers any permission, consent or approval or issues any licence, registration certificate or permit,
furnishes any information,

processes an application for any permission, consent, approval, licence, registration certificate or permit (including by making an inspection or conducting an audit in connection with the application),
provides advice on request (including by way of lecture or seminar), or
provides administrative services on request (including photocopying and the like),

under this Act or the regulations, the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 or the regulations under those Acts or in connection with any national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve or Aboriginal area, the Secretary or an officer of the Service may make, demand, levy and recover such charges and fees as may be prescribed or where no charge or fee is prescribed such charges and fees as may be fixed by the Secretary, subject to the maximum (if any) prescribed.

Nothing in this section prevents the Secretary or an officer of the Service making, demanding, levying or recovering separate charges or fees in respect of the same person for the supply of different things or carrying out of different activities.

The services referred to in subsection (1) include, but are not limited to, health or building services provided or maintained by the Secretary in a national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve or Aboriginal area.

heading.b: Overdue community service contributions, charges, fees and other money

block.txt: Interest on overdue money payable in respect of—
leases, licences, permits or occupancies within reserved or dedicated lands, and
leases and licences granted under section 149 (4), and
royalties, fees and charges under this Act, the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995, and
franchises granted under section 152, and
easements or rights of way granted under section 153, and
community service contributions under section 140,
shall be payable in accordance with this section.

If payment of the whole or any part of an amount payable in respect of a matter referred to in subsection (1) has not been made at the date when the amount was due, the balance due from time to time after that date is to attract interest—
except as provided by paragraph (b)—calculated at the prescribed rate, or
in the case of interest payable under a lease, agreement or other instrument the terms of which fix a rate of interest that is higher than the prescribed rate—calculated at that higher rate.
If the Minister, on the recommendation of the Secretary, is satisfied that circumstances warrant it, the Minister may—
direct that an amount due shall not attract interest in accordance with this section, or
grant an extension of time after the due date during which the amount payable or due for the time being will not attract interest, or
remit the payment of the whole or any part of any interest payable under this section.
No refund shall be made as a consequence of a remission under subsection (3) (c).

This section applies to overdue money payable before, as well as on or after, the commencement of this section, in so far as it is due on and after that commencement, and so applies notwithstanding the terms of any lease, agreement or other instrument under which the money is payable.
Interest payable under this section may be recovered in the same way as the money in respect of which it is payable.

The Service is to include a statement of its operations and expenditure in connection with lands reserved or dedicated under Part 4A in the annual reporting information prepared for it under the Government Sector Finance Act 2018.

content.txt: s 144B: Ins 1996 No 142, Sch 1 [41]. Subst 2018 No 70, Sch 4.72.

heading.b: Acquisition of land for reservation or other purposes

block.txt: The Minister may, for the purpose of obtaining land for reservation under Part 4 or Part 4A, of conserving threatened species, populations or ecological communities, or their habitats or of preserving, protecting and preventing damage to Aboriginal objects or Aboriginal places—
on behalf of Her Majesty, enter into and give effect to an agreement for the vesting in, or surrender to, Her Majesty of any land, or
acquire land by agreement or by compulsory process in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.

heading.b: Acquisition or occupation of lands for certain purposes

block.txt: For the purpose of—
improving access to any land reserved or dedicated or acquired under this Act,
the management, maintenance or improvement of any such land, or
carrying out works for any of those purposes,
the Minister may—

on behalf of Her Majesty, enter into, and give effect to, an agreement for the vesting in, surrender to, or leasing to, Her Majesty, or for the occupation under licence, of any land adjoining or in the vicinity of the land so reserved or dedicated, or

acquire any land (including an interest in land) adjoining or in the vicinity of the land so reserved or dedicated by agreement or by compulsory process in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.
For the purpose of obtaining lands for use in connection with the administration of this Act, the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995, the Minister may—
on behalf of Her Majesty, enter into, and give effect to, an agreement for the vesting in, surrender to, or leasing to, Her Majesty, or for the occupation under licence, of any land, or
acquire land (including an interest in land) by agreement or by compulsory process in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.

The Minister may, on behalf of the Crown, acquire land (including an interest in land) for the purpose of a future lease grant or dealing by agreement or by compulsory process in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.
An acquisition for a future lease grant or dealing is an acquisition—
to enable the reservation or dedication of land under this Act and the exercise of powers, authorities, duties and functions conferred or imposed by or under this Act in relation to the land, or
to enable the exercise of powers, authorities, duties and functions conferred or imposed by or under this Act in relation to land already reserved or dedicated under this Act.

The publication in the Gazette of an acquisition notice under section 19 of the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991 for a purpose that is described as a future lease grant or dealing does not—
to the extent to which the land referred to in the acquisition notice was Crown land immediately before the publication of the acquisition notice, affect the status of the land as Crown land, or

operate to revoke any reservation as national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve or karst conservation reserve of the land referred to in the acquisition notice.
Nothing in this section is taken to mean that the Minister cannot exercise functions in relation to land under this Act unless the Minister first compulsorily acquires the land concerned.
Subsection (2A) does not limit the purposes for which land may be acquired under section 145 or any other provision of this Act.

The Minister or Secretary may, for the purpose of the management, maintenance or improvement of any land reserved or dedicated under this Act, enter into and give effect to an agreement with the owner or lessee of the land, as the case requires, concerning the management or care of any land adjoining or in the vicinity of land so reserved or dedicated.

For the purposes of the Public Works Act 1912, any acquisition of land under section 145 or 146 is taken to be for an authorised work and the Minister is, in relation to that authorised work, taken to be the Constructing Authority.
Sections 34, 35, 36 and 37 of the Public Works Act 1912 do not apply in respect of works constructed under this Act.

heading.b: Power of Minister to accept gifts

block.txt: The Minister may acquire, by gift inter vivos, devise or bequest, any property for the purposes of this Act, the Wilderness Act 1987 or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 and may agree to the condition of any such gift, devise or bequest.
The rule of law against remoteness of vesting shall not apply to any such condition to which the Minister has agreed.
Where the Minister acquires property under subsection (1)—
neither an instrument that effects the acquisition nor any agreement pursuant to which the property is acquired is chargeable with duty under the Stamp Duties Act 1920, and
the property, or the value of property, shall not be included in the dutiable estate of the donor or testator for the purposes of assessing death duty under that Act.

Notwithstanding anything in Part 4 or Part 4A, lands acquired under this section must not be reserved as, or as part of, a national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve or karst conservation reserve in contravention of any such condition to which the Minister has agreed.

Subject to any conditions of a gift or an agreement by or under which any such property may have been acquired, the Minister may sell, grant leases of, dispose of or otherwise deal with any lands or other property—
acquired by the Minister, otherwise than on behalf of Her Majesty, under this Part or another provision of this Act, or

acquired by the Minister on behalf of Her Majesty for the purposes of this Act or the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 by purchase with money from the Fund, by exchange of any property so purchased or by gift,
or any interest in any such lands or other property.

Nothing in this section applies to or in respect of lands while reserved as, or as part of, a national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve or karst conservation reserve.
Nothing in this section affects the operation of Part 4A.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may—
for use in connection with the administration of this Act grant a lease of, or a licence with respect to, lands referred to in section 146 (2).

heading.b: Minister to be corporation sole for certain purposes

block.txt: For the purposes of the exercise and performance of the Minister’s authorities, duties and functions under Part 4A and this Part and under any other provisions of this or any other Act that are identified (by those provisions) for the purposes of this section, the Minister is hereby constituted a corporation sole under the name of “Minister administering the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974”.
The corporation sole constituted by this section—
has perpetual succession,
shall have an official seal,
may take proceedings and be proceeded against in the corporate name,

may, in accordance with this Act (or with such provisions of any other Act as are identified as referred to in subsection (1)), purchase, exchange, hold, dispose of and otherwise deal with property, and
may do and suffer all other things that a body corporate generally may, by law, do and suffer and that are necessary for or incidental to the purposes for which the corporation sole is constituted.

The seal of the corporation sole so constituted shall not be affixed to any instrument or document except in the presence of the Minister, and the Minister shall attest by the Minister’s signature the fact and date of the affixing of the seal.
All courts and persons acting judicially—
shall take judicial notice of the seal of the corporation sole so constituted that has been affixed to any instrument or document, and
shall until the contrary is proved presume that seal was properly affixed.
In this Part—
existing building or structure means—
in relation to land reserved under this Act before the commencement of this section, a building or structure in existence on the land at that commencement, or
in relation to land that becomes reserved under this Act on or after the commencement of this section, a building or structure in existence on the land at the time of that reservation.

reserve means a national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve or Aboriginal area (and includes any such land reserved under Part 4A).

heading.b: Leases and licences of reserved lands

block.txt: The Minister may grant a lease or licence of land within a reserve (including any buildings or structures on the land).
A lease or licence granted under this section may authorise any one or more of the following—
the exclusive use of the land, buildings and structures concerned,
the erection of a new building or structure on the land concerned,
the modification of an existing building or structure on the land concerned.
Without limiting section 2A, in determining whether to grant a lease or licence of land under this section, the Minister is to give effect to the objects of this Act.
Section 2A (1) (d) provides that it is an object of this Act that the management of reserved land be in accordance with the applicable management principles.

Section 81A makes it clear that Part 5 (Plans of management) has effect in any part of a reserve that is the subject of a lease or licence under this Part. Section 151C also provides that it is a condition of every lease or licence of land granted under this section that the lessee or licensee must ensure that the provisions of this Act, the regulations and the relevant plan of management are complied with.

heading.b: Purposes for which a lease or licence may be granted

block.txt: A lease or licence of land (other than a nature reserve) may only be granted under section 151 for one or more of the following purposes—
the provision of buildings for use in connection with any of the following—
the protection or preservation of land from fire,
the provision of services relating to the work of rendering first aid to, and the transport of, sick and injured persons,
a surf life-saving club,
any purpose of a similar nature,
the provision of research facilities or activities for natural heritage (including natural phenomena) and cultural heritage,
to enable activities of a recreational, educational or cultural nature to be carried out and the provision of facilities for that purpose,
to enable sporting activities to be carried out and the provision of temporary facilities for that purpose,
to enable activities for natural heritage management, cultural heritage management, park management or fire management to be carried out and the provision of facilities for that purpose,
to enable Aboriginal cultural activities to be carried out and the provision of facilities for that purpose,
subject to section 151I (Restrictions on grant of lease for residential accommodation), the provision of residential accommodation,
any other purpose that is—
consistent with the relevant management principles for the land set out in Division 2 of Part 4, and
identified in the relevant plan of management as being a permissible purpose for the land concerned,

heading.b: Purposes related to the sustainable visitor or tourist use and enjoyment of reserved land

block.txt: the provision of accommodation for visitors and tourists,
the provision of the following facilities if the facilities are ancillary to accommodation facilities for visitors or tourists—
retail outlets,
facilities to enable the hosting of conferences or functions,
facilities to enable activities of a sporting nature to be carried out,
the provision of facilities and amenities for visitors and tourists, including the following facilities—
information centres and booking outlets,
restaurants, cafes, kiosks and other food outlets,
the provision of the following facilities if the facilities are ancillary to facilities and amenities for visitors and tourists—
retail outlets,
facilities to enable the hosting of conferences or functions,

heading.b: Adaptive reuse and use of modified natural areas

block.txt: any purpose that enables the adaptive reuse of an existing building or structure or the use of a modified natural area.
See section 5 (1) for the definitions of “adaptive reuse” and “modified natural area”.

A lease or licence of land within a nature reserve may only be granted under section 151 for a purpose that is consistent with the relevant management principles for nature reserves set out in section 30J.

In addition to the purposes set out in subsection (1), a lease or licence of land (other than a nature reserve) may be granted under section 151 to enable any activity or development in a ski resort area (within the meaning of Part 8A of Schedule 6 to the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979) that is permitted by an environmental planning instrument specifically applying to ski resort areas.

A licence of land under section 151 for the purpose of a conference, function or event must not be granted if the licence authorises the use of the land for a cumulative period that exceeds 3 months in any 12 month period.
The Minister must not grant a lease of land under section 151 for any purpose referred to in subsection (1) (b) that authorises the erection of a new building or structure on the land unless—
the purpose for which the lease is to be granted is identified in the relevant plan of management as being a permissible purpose for the land concerned, and
the general location for any such new building or structure is identified in that plan of management.

heading.b: Matters that Minister must consider before granting lease or licence

block.txt: The Minister must not grant a lease or licence of land (including any buildings or structures on the land) under section 151 unless the Minister is satisfied that—
the purpose for which the lease or licence is granted is compatible with the natural and cultural values of—
the land to be leased or licensed, and
land reserved under this Act in the vicinity of that land, and
the lease or licence provides for the sustainable and efficient use of natural resources, energy and water, and

in relation to any lease or licence that authorises the erection of a new building or structure on the land or the modification of an existing building or structure on the land—the authorised development or activity is appropriate in relation to the built form and scale of the building or structure, including its bulk, height, footprint, setbacks and density.
In determining whether the Minister is satisfied in relation to any of the matters referred to in subsection (1), the Minister is to have regard to—
the assessment criteria adopted by the Secretary under subsection (3), and
in relation to a proposal to grant a lease of land—a report prepared by the Secretary that addresses the relevant matters referred to in subsection (1) in light of those assessment criteria.
The Secretary—
must adopt assessment criteria relating to the matters referred to in subsection (1), and
may vary those criteria, but only if—
the Secretary has consulted with the Council, and
the Council has advised the Secretary that the proposed variation, on balance, improves or maintains the environmental outcomes provided for under the existing criteria.
The assessment criteria are to be published on the Department’s website.
This section does not apply to the following—
a lease or licence of land within a ski resort area within the meaning of Part 8A of Schedule 6 to the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979,
a renewal of a lease of land granted in accordance with an option to renew a current lease,
a renewal of a lease of land (otherwise than in accordance with an option to renew), but only if—
the renewed lease is on substantially the same terms and conditions as the current lease, and
the term of the lease (including any options to renew) does not exceed 10 years, and
there have been no significant breaches of the current lease, this Act or the regulations during the term of the current lease.

heading.b: Leases and licences subject to conditions

block.txt: A lease or licence under section 149, 151 or 151H may be granted subject to conditions.

It is a condition of every lease or licence of land granted under section 151 that the lessee or licensee must ensure that the provisions of this Act, the regulations and the plan of management for the reserve in which the land is situated are complied with in relation to the land.

heading.b: Special provisions relating to leases and licences of karst conservation reserves

block.txt: The Minister is to include in every lease or licence of land within a karst conservation reserve granted under section 151 a condition requiring—
the lessee or licensee (in relation to the lands leased or licensed) to comply with the relevant environmental performance standards set out in the plan of management for the reserve, and

the environmental performance of the lessee or licensee (in relation to the lands leased or licensed) to be measured against the relevant environmental performance indicators set out in that plan of management.
The Secretary is (in relation to a lease or licence to which subsection (1) applies)—
to monitor—
the lessee’s or licensee’s compliance with the relevant environmental performance standards set out in the relevant plan of management, and
the lessee’s or licensee’s environmental performance as measured against the relevant environmental performance indicators set out in that plan of management, and
to report on the results of that monitoring, annually, by—
recording the results in the register kept under section 151J, and
placing the results on the Department’s website.

heading.b: Special provisions relating to leases and licences of Aboriginal land

block.txt: The Minister may only grant a lease or licence under section 151 of land reserved under Part 4A with the concurrence of the relevant board of management for the land concerned.
The Minister must not grant a lease or licence under section 151 of land reserved under Part 4A contrary to the terms of the lease of the land to the Minister under that Part.

heading.b: Public consultation regarding grant of leases and licences

block.txt: Before granting a lease or licence under section 151 or 151H, the Minister must cause notice of the proposed lease or licence to be published—

in a manner that the Minister is satisfied is likely to bring the notice to the attention of members of the public in the area in which the land is located, and also on the Department’s website, if the proposed lease or licence—
is for a purpose for which the land (including any buildings or structures on the land) has previously not been used or occupied, or
authorises the erection of a temporary building or structure on the land concerned, and

in a manner that the Minister is satisfied is likely to bring the notice to the attention of members of the public both generally and in the area in which the land is located, and also on the Department’s website, if the proposed lease or licence—
authorises the erection of a new permanent building or structure on the land concerned, or
authorises a significant modification of an existing building or structure on the land concerned or any other significant permanent physical change to the land concerned.
A notice under subsection (1) must contain the following—
sufficient information to identify the land concerned,
the purposes for which the land and any building or structure on the land is proposed to be used,
the term of the proposed lease or licence (taking into account any option to renew),
the name of the person to whom the lease or licence is proposed to be granted,
the closing date for making submissions on the proposal, being a date not earlier than—
in relation to a notice under subsection (1) (a)—14 days after the date on which the notice was first published, or
in relation to a notice under subsection (1) (b)—28 days after the date on which the notice was first published,
the address to which submissions are to be sent,
any other information that the Minister considers relevant to the consideration of the proposal.

The Minister, on request, is to provide such further information, as the Minister considers reasonably practicable, describing the proposed lease or licence. The information provided must not include any commercial in confidence information.
Further information provided under this subsection could include drawings or diagrams describing the proposed lease or licence.
The Minister may hold a public hearing into any proposed lease or licence under this Part if the Minister thinks it appropriate to do so.
Before determining whether or not to grant a lease or licence under section 151 or 151H, the Minister must take into account—
any submissions received before the notified closing date for submissions under subsection (2) (e), and
if relevant, any report from, or submissions received at, a public hearing.
This section does not apply to a proposal to grant a lease or licence of land if—
the proposed lease or licence authorises the land concerned to be used or occupied for a total period that does not exceed 31 days, or

the proposed lease or licence relates to land reserved under Part 4A and authorises the land concerned to be used or occupied for any community development purpose prescribed by the regulations under section 72AB(5), or

within the 2 years prior to the proposed grant of the lease or licence, a public consultation has occurred in relation to development or an activity that is substantially the same as the use of the land that is to be authorised by the proposed lease or licence.

For example, a public consultation may have been undertaken under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 for approval or consent to the erection and use of a building for a cafe. In that case, public consultation is not necessary under this section in relation to a proposed lease of the building to operate that cafe.

heading.b: Reference of certain proposed leases and licences for advice

block.txt: The Minister—
must refer a proposal to lease or licence land under section 151 to the Council for advice if the proposed lease or licence—
authorises the erection of a new permanent building or structure on the land concerned, or
authorises a significant modification of an existing building or structure on the land concerned or any other significant permanent physical change to the land concerned, or
is for a term that exceeds 10 years (including any option to renew), and
must refer a proposal to lease land under section 151H to the Council for advice, and
may refer any other proposal to lease or licence land under this Part to the Council for advice if the Minister thinks it appropriate to do so.
The Minister may refer a proposal to lease or licence land under this Part to the Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Advisory Committee for advice if the Minister thinks it appropriate to do so.

The Minister may refer a proposal to lease or licence land within a karst conservation reserve under this Part to the Karst Management Advisory Committee for advice if the Minister thinks it appropriate to do so.

Before determining whether or not to grant a lease or licence under this Part, the Minister must, if the Minister referred the proposal to the Council, the Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Advisory Committee or the Karst Management Advisory Committee, take into account any advice received from the body concerned within 28 days of the reference.

heading.b: New head leases for certain lands

block.txt: The Minister may grant leases (in this section referred to as head leases) in respect of the lands the subject of any or all of the leases mentioned in Schedule 15, whether or not those lands are still the subject of the leases so mentioned.
On the granting of a head lease, the following provisions have effect with respect to such of the leases mentioned in Schedule 15 as apply to the land the subject of the head lease—
the lease is taken to be varied by substituting the name of the head lessee for that of the lessor,
the lease is taken to become a sublease (in this section referred to as a statutory sublease) of the head lease,
except as otherwise provided by the regulations—the lease continues to have effect according to its tenor,

any proceedings under the lease in relation to any matter arising before the head lease was granted are to be commenced or maintained by or against the lessor as if the lease had not been varied as referred to in paragraph (a).

If a head lease is granted to a person in respect of land the subject of a lease mentioned in Schedule 15 of which the person is the sole lessee, the lease so mentioned is, by virtue of the granting of the head lease, extinguished.
A head lease is taken to include a condition to the effect that the head lessee must not—
assign or mortgage the head lessee’s interest in the lease to any other person, or
exercise any right of forfeiture or termination in respect of any statutory sublease of the lease, or
vary any rent payable under any statutory sublease of the lease,
except with the prior consent in writing of the Minister, and that any purported assignment, mortgage, forfeiture, termination or variation of rent that does not have such consent is void.

A head lease is not affected merely because a lease mentioned in Schedule 15 ceases to have effect (whether by reason of expiry, surrender, termination, forfeiture or otherwise) while the head lease is in force.

If a head lease ceases to have effect (whether by reason of expiry, surrender, termination, forfeiture or otherwise) the following provisions have effect with respect to any statutory sublease of the head lease—
the sublease is taken to be varied by substituting the title of the Minister for the name of the head lessee,
the sublease is taken to cease to be a statutory sublease and to become a lease granted under section 151,
the lease continues to have effect according to its tenor,

any proceedings under the sublease in relation to any matter arising before the head lease ceased to have effect are to be commenced or maintained against the head lessee as if the lease had not been varied as referred to in paragraph (a).
No duty is payable under the Stamp Duties Act 1920 in respect of a variation referred to in subsection (2) (a) or (6) (a).
The operation of this section is not to be regarded—
as a breach of contract or confidence or otherwise as a civil wrong, or
as a breach of a contractual provision prohibiting, restricting or regulating the assignment or transfer of a lease or statutory sublease, or
as giving rise to any remedy by a party to an instrument, or as causing or permitting the termination of any instrument, because of a variation referred to in subsection (2) (a) or (6) (a).
No attornment to a head lessee by a statutory sublessee is required.
The regulations may amend Schedule 15—
by omitting the matter relating to any lease mentioned in that Schedule, or
by varying the matter relating to any lease mentioned in that Schedule, or
by inserting matter relating to any other lease (not being a head lease) in relation to land in, or in the vicinity of, Perisher Valley, Smiggin Holes or Guthega.

A head lease granted in respect of land the subject of a lease mentioned in Schedule 15 is not affected merely because the matter relating to the lease so mentioned is omitted from that Schedule, or is varied, while the head lease is in force.

content.txt: s 151H (previously s 151A): Ins 1990 No 106, Sch 1 (2). Renumbered 2010 No 41, Sch 1 [18].

heading.b: Restrictions on grant of lease for residential accommodation

block.txt: The Minister must not grant a lease under section 151 or 151H for the purpose of permanent residential occupation unless the lease—
provides accommodation to an officer of the Service in the vicinity of the officer’s place of employment, or
facilitates—
the maintenance and security of the reserve, and buildings and facilities on or in the reserve, or facilities passing through the reserve such as a road, transmission lines and pipelines, or
the provision of services to tourists and visitors to the reserve,
the provision of educational and research facilities in the reserve, or
is for the occupation of buildings in an historic site or land reserved under Part 4A, or
is of a class prescribed for the purposes of this section.
A regulation must not be made for the purposes of subsection (1) (d) (not being a principal statutory rule within the meaning of the Subordinate Legislation Act 1989) unless the Minister has—
caused notice of the draft regulation to be published in a manner that the Minister is satisfied is likely to bring the notice to the attention of members of the public, and

invited the public and the Council to comment on the draft regulation with the closing date for the making of submissions being not earlier than 45 days after the date of publication of the notice, and
taken into account any submissions from the Council or the public received before the notified closing date for submissions.
The validity of a regulation made for the purposes of subsection (1) (d) is not affected by a failure of the Minister to comply with subsection (2) (c).

content.txt: s 151I (previously s 151C): Ins 2001 No 130, Sch 1 [61]. Renumbered 2010 No 41, Sch 1 [18]. Am 2010 No 41, Sch 1 [20]; 2018 No 25, Sch 2.22 [3].

heading.b: Register of certain interests to be publicly available

block.txt: Information on leases granted under this Act, licences granted under section 153D and every easement or right of way granted under this Act—
is to be recorded in a register that is to be kept in the head office of the Service and made available to the public, free of charge, during ordinary office hours, and
is to be placed on the Service’s website.
Information to be included on the register and website is to include the following—
the name of the person to whom the lease, licence, easement or right of way has been granted,
the term of years of the lease, licence, easement or right of way (including any option to renew),
the location of the land to which the lease, licence, easement or right of way relates,
the purpose for which the lease, licence, easement or right of way has been granted,

information as to the terms and conditions of the lease, licence, easement or right of way, except information that the Secretary would be prevented from disclosing under the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009 or the Privacy and Personal Information Protection Act 1998.

content.txt: s 151J (previously s 151D): Ins 2001 No 130, Sch 1 [61]. Am 2003 No 37, Sch 1 [1] [2]; 2009 No 54, Sch 2.31 [1]. Renumbered 2010 No 41, Sch 1 [18].

block.txt: The Secretary may grant licences to carry on trades, businesses or occupations within a national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve or Aboriginal area.

Subject to any regulations, the Minister may prohibit the carrying on of any trade, business or occupation within a national park, historic site, state conservation area, regional park, nature reserve, karst conservation reserve or Aboriginal area otherwise than by some person licensed by the Secretary.
